placements.title: Deployment moves from unsigned trust to mandatory, owned, environment-wide signed-manifest gating
placements.frame: Does this expression establish, scope, or justify a requirement that release artifacts carry verified signed provenance before deployment, and who is accountable for enforcing it?
placements.why: src-1 states the gate as a standing rule ('now requires a signed release manifest before it ships'); src-3/src-4/src-5 restate and extend it as a structured specification (Gate/Scope/Owner) in the same protocol register — one performed policy: what the gate is, where it applies (staging and production), who owns it (Quinton Fairweather). This is a subject future release-train envelopes will keep feeding (gate exceptions, scope changes, ownership handoffs), not a one-time fact, so it earns a leaf per the narrative grain test. src-2's 'two unsigned artifacts reach staging last quarter' is the evidentiary rationale for the same gate ('the whole reason for the gate') — a fact that evidences this leaf's necessity rather than a standalone occurrence, so it joins as supporting content rather than minting its own leaf. No existing narrative leaf exists in this repo to reuse, so this is a fresh mint under the newly-minted Architecture strata.
